logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of iridium complexes was determined using the shake-flask method. Initially, the iridium complexes (10 mM in DMSO) were diluted into 0.15 mM in three different mixtures: (i) a1: 1 ratio of octanol: PBS, (ii) a 2: 1 ratio of octanol: PBS, and (iii) a 1: 2 ratio of octanol: PBS. The mixtures were shaken vigorously, and the solutions were allowed to settle for approximately 30 min until complete phase separation occurred. After separation, each phase was analyzed by UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy. The concentration of the iridium complex in each phase was determined using a calibration curve. The partition coefficients of the iridium complexes were then calculated using the formula Log P = log ([Ir]Oct / [Ir]PBS), where [Ir]Oct represents the concentration of the iridium in octanol, and [Ir]PBS represents the concentration of iridium in PBS. The Log P reportedis the average value obtained from triplicate runs.

The lipophilicity of iridium complexes was determined using the shake-flask method. Initially, the iridium complexes (10 mM in DMSO) were diluted to 0.15 mM in three different mixtures: (i) a 1:1 ratio of octanol:PBS, (ii) a 2: 1 ratio of octanol:PBS, and (iii) a 1: 2 ratio of octanol:PBS. The mixtures were shaken vigorously, and the solutions were allowed to settle for approximately 30 min until complete phase separation occurred. After separation, each phase was analyzed by UV-Vis absorption spectroscopy. The concentration of the iridium complex in each phase was determined using a calibration curve. The partition coefficients of the iridium complexes were then calculatedusing the formula Log P = log ([Ir]Oct/[Ir]PBS), where [Ir]Oct represents the concentration of the iridium in octanol, and [Ir]PBS represents the concentration of iridium in PBS. The Log P reported is the average value obtained from triplicate runs

Octanol-saturated water (OSW) and water-saturated octanol (WSO) were prepared using analytical grade octanol and 0.25 M aqueous NaCl (to suppress aquation of the Ir complexes). Aliquots of the Ir complex stock solution in WSO were added to equal volumes of OSW, shaken in a VWR mini shaker for 6 h and then left undisturbed for the layers to separate (shake-flask method). The octanol layer was carefully separated into test tubes, dried over Na2SO4 and then analyzed by UV-vis spectroscopy at ambient temperature. The concentrations of the Ir complex in the octanol phase were determined using a calibration curve generated using a standard solution of the Ir complexes (0, 0.025, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 mM) in octanol. The concentrations of the Ir complex in water were calculated by following [Ir]water = ([Ir]total added x V(octanol+water) - [Ir]octanol x V(octanol))/V(water). The log of the partition coefficients (LogP) were calculated using the following equation: LogP = log([Ir]octanol/[Ir]water). The logP values shown represent the average number obtained from duplicate experiments performed in octanol:water (1:2) with a total volume of 12 mL.
